title: IPTV Technical Guides: M3U, EPG, XMLTV & Formats
description: Plain-English explanations of how IPTV works under the hood: M3U playlists, EPG and XMLTV guides, tvg-id tags, stream formats and validation.
intro: IPTV is just television delivered over an internet connection, but the file formats and acronyms around it (M3U, M3U8, EPG, XMLTV, HLS, tvg-id) trip people up. These guides explain each piece, show real examples and help you validate your own files.

faq.question: What is the difference between M3U and M3U8?
faq.answer: M3U8 is simply an M3U playlist saved with UTF-8 encoding. In practice M3U8 is also the extension used for HLS (HTTP Live Streaming) manifests, which are a specialised form of playlist.

faq.question: Do I need an EPG to use IPTV?
faq.answer: No. An EPG (electronic programme guide) only adds programme titles and times. Streams play without it, but most players look and feel much better with a matching XMLTV guide.
